title.en: Vertebral column regions, curves and disc structure

summary: Build a segmented spine whose regional counts and curvatures stay correct while an authored flexion envelope is explored.
objective: Create a vertebral column I can bend within an authored limit while keeping regional labels, curvature naming and disc structure visible.
intent_signals: Show how the spine is segmented and where its curves are.
Explain the parts of an intervertebral disc in three dimensions.
example_prompts: Create a labelled vertebral column with regional colours, the four curves and a cutaway disc.
Let me flex the lumbar region within a stated limit and see the disc cross-section respond.
negative_signals: Not a validated range-of-motion or spinal load model; no disc pressure or injury prediction.
Not a patient-specific or imaging-derived spine.
not_for: Not a validated range-of-motion or spinal load model; no disc pressure or injury prediction.
Not a patient-specific or imaging-derived spine.

entities.name: Vertebra stack
entities.guidance: Model each vertebra as a body, pedicles and a spinous process with its own region tag and index; do not repeat one identical mesh through all regions.

entities.name: Intervertebral discs
entities.guidance: Build each disc as a layered anulus ring around a distinct inner nucleus volume so a cutaway reveals two materials, not a painted stripe.

entities.name: Curve reference
entities.guidance: Draw the column centre curve with the four curvature spans named separately, plus an upright reference silhouette that stays visible during flexion.

state_contract.model: Ordered vertebra list with region tags and per-joint angles bounded by an authored envelope; disc geometry is derived from adjacent vertebra transforms. No load, stress or tissue model.
state_contract.authority: The joint angle list is authoritative. Disc wedge shape and the centre curve are recomputed from it; the reference silhouette is a stored pose, never a live copy.
actions: Flex or extend a selected region within the authored envelope.
Open a disc cutaway at a chosen level.
Toggle region labels and the neutral reference silhouette.
Reset all joint angles to the neutral pose.

invariants: Regional counts stay fixed under any pose: seven cervical, twelve thoracic and five lumbar vertebrae.
Disc volume is not created or destroyed by the display: a wedge that opens on one side must close on the other.
Joint angles clamp at the authored envelope instead of continuing to rotate.
motion_guidance: Distribute a bend across the vertebrae of the selected region rather than hinging at a single joint.
Ease the motion and keep the neutral silhouette on screen so the change stays measurable.
known_limits: The flexion envelope is an authored teaching choice, not a sourced clinical range of motion, and it is marked as such in the defaults; only the counts and the curvature classification come from the cited section.

Discs are derived from adjacent pairs in the modelled chain. The real column has no intervertebral disc between the atlas and the axis, so a model that includes C1 must mark that joint disc-free rather than generating a disc for every adjacent pair.
Ligaments, muscles and the spinal cord are omitted or shown only as context.
Authored guidance only: no scene runtime, rendering or numerical calibration has been run for this recipe.

claims.statement: The vertebral column contains seven cervical vertebrae, twelve thoracic vertebrae designated T1 to T12 and five lumbar vertebrae, with a sacrum formed from five fused sacral vertebrae and a coccyx from four small coccygeal vertebrae.
claims.scope: Typical adult counts as taught; numerical variants exist in individuals and are not modelled.

claims.statement: The thoracic and sacrococcygeal curves are primary curves retained from fetal curvature, while the cervical and lumbar curves are secondary curves that develop after birth.
claims.scope: Naming and developmental grouping of the four curves; no angle values are asserted.

claims.statement: An intervertebral disc has a tough fibrous outer anulus fibrosus and a softer, gel-like nucleus pulposus with a high water content that resists compression.
claims.scope: Two-component disc composition; no stiffness, pressure or degeneration behaviour is claimed.

object_craft.structure: Distinct body, pedicle and process masses per vertebra with region-specific proportions; cervical bodies smaller than lumbar bodies.
object_craft.material: Dense matte bone with slight porosity variation between cortical rim and interior cut faces; region tint applied as a thin overlay so it can be switched off.
object_craft.articulation: Each vertebra is a child of a per-joint pivot placed at the disc centre, so a joint angle moves everything above it.

object_craft.structure: Concentric anulus lamellae around a rounded nucleus volume, with a capped cutaway surface at the inspected level.
object_craft.material: Fibrous, directionally shaded anulus against a smoother translucent nucleus; the two materials must differ in roughness, not only in colour.
object_craft.articulation: Disc shape is driven by adjacent vertebra transforms: it wedges as the joint rotates.

physical_contract.scope: Authored articulation within a declared envelope and cutaway presentation; no tissue mechanics, contact or load.
checks: Angles clamp at the envelope and reset returns exactly to neutral.
Region counts and labels are unchanged after any pose change.

defaults.rationale: The regional counts, the sacral and coccygeal element counts and the primary and secondary curvature classification are already carried by this record's claims, so no new source was needed; the defaults turn them into the totals a build can assert while posing. Two entries are authored and labelled: the per-joint flexion envelope, because the cited section gives no range of motion, and the disc wedge proportions, because it describes the anulus and nucleus without dimensions. Tunable in the envelope and the display proportions only; the counts are not settings.

sacral_vertebrae_fused.note: sourced; fused into the sacrum, so they contribute no mobile joints

per_joint_flexion_envelope.note: authored teaching envelope, applied as plus or minus about neutral; the cited section states no range of motion

disc_anulus_fraction_of_disc_radius.note: authored display proportion; the section describes a tough outer anulus fibrosus around a gel-like nucleus pulposus without dimensions

curve_angles.note: the section names the curves and their origin, not their magnitudes

equations: joints in a chain of n vertebrae = n - 1
total vertebral elements = presacral + fused sacral + coccygeal

worked_example.inputs: The sourced regional counts, and a flexion request of 12 degrees at one lumbar joint against the authored 8 degree envelope
worked_example.expected: 24 presacral vertebrae and 33 vertebral elements in total; 23 joints in the presacral chain, of which the atlas-axis joint must be marked disc-free rather than generating a disc; the 12 degree request applies as exactly 8 degrees and reset returns the joint to exactly 0
worked_example.derivation: 7 + 12 + 5 = 24 presacral vertebrae; adding the 5 fused sacral and 4 coccygeal elements gives 24 + 5 + 4 = 33. A chain of 24 vertebrae has 24 - 1 = 23 joints; the count of generated discs is therefore 23 minus the joints declared disc-free, which is 22 for a model that starts at C1. Clamping: clamp(12, -8, +8) = 8, so the pose stops at the envelope instead of continuing to rotate, and because the clamp is applied to the requested angle rather than accumulated, reset yields exactly 0 rather than a residue. Region counts are asserted after every pose change: a display that reparents or drops a vertebra will change one of 7, 12 or 5 while the total still looks plausible, which is why all three are checked, not just the sum.

tolerance.counts: exact integers, re-asserted after any pose change
tolerance.angle_deg: 1e-6 deg on the clamp boundary; the clamped value must equal the envelope exactly, not approach it
tolerance.disc_volume: a wedge that opens on one side must close on the other to within 1 percent of the disc's neutral volume
